title: Oklo vs AST SpaceMobile: Two Pre-Revenue Moonshots Powering the AI-and-Space Trade
excerpt: Oklo just hit a nuclear milestone that took under a year to achieve, while AST SpaceMobile absorbed a nine-figure launch loss and kept building anyway. One b...

Quick Read

  • OKLO's Groves reactor hit first criticality while ASTS absorbed a $126M BB7 launch loss, both racing to build AI-era infrastructure.

  • ASTS's $2.29B cash pile and $1.30B backlog offer a clearer commercialization bridge, while OKLO's 2027 first-power target demands significant patience.

  • It sounds nuts, but SoFi1 is giving new Active Invest users up to $3,000 in stock for a limited time, and all it takes is a $50 deposit to get started.2 See for yourself (Sponsor)

Oklo (NYSE: OKLO) and AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ: ASTS) just gave investors two very different views of what an early-stage AI infrastructure bet looks like.

Oklo posted its first-ever quarterly revenue of $1.21 million. AST SpaceMobile printed $31.52 million alongside a nine-figure launch loss. Both stories are about building infrastructure the AI era needs, but the pacing could not be more different.

Groves Goes Critical While BB7 Weighs on the Sky

Oklo's quarter was defined by an operational milestone, not the income statement. The Groves reactor achieved first criticality in under a year, a moment retail investors amplified across r/stocks, r/stockmarket, and r/investing at a bullish sentiment score of 72.

The revenue beat versus a $0.12 million consensus mattered less than proof the Aurora program is moving from paper to power. The EPS miss of -$0.28 against a -$0.16 estimate did dampen enthusiasm, though.

AST SpaceMobile's quarter looked heavier. Revenue missed by 8.36% and the GAAP loss came in at -$0.77 versus a -$0.29 consensus, a 168.01% shortfall driven by a $125.9 million loss on involuntary conversion tied to the BB7 launch incident. Yet the network keeps expanding.

CEO Abel Avellan told investors, "our space-based cellular broadband network has now grown to 13 spacecraft in orbit, each the largest ever in low Earth orbit", with BlueBirds 14, 15, and 16 ready to ship.

Oklo sells electrons. Its Aurora powerhouse design expanded from 50 MW to 75 MW to court hyperscalers, and the anchor deal is a 12 GW master power agreement with Switch.

CEO Jacob DeWitte framed the moment plainly: "The world is catching up to what we've known all along: nuclear power is essential to a clean, dependable, and scalable energy future." Oklo builds, owns, and operates the reactors, which lengthens the cash-out cycle but keeps long-term economics inside the house.

快速阅读

  • OKLO 的格罗夫斯反应堆达到了首次临界点，而 ASTS 吸收了 1.26 亿美元的 BB7 发射损失，两者都在竞相建设人工智能时代的基础设施。
  • ASTS 的 $2.29B 现金储备和 $1.30B 积压订单提供了更清晰的商业化桥梁，而 OKLO 的 2027 年第一电力目标需要极大的耐心。
  • 这听起来很疯狂，但 SoFi1 正在限时为新的 Active Invest 用户提供高达 3,000 美元的股票，只需缴纳 50 美元即可开始使用。2 亲自体验（赞助商）

Oklo（纽约证券交易所股票代码：OKLO）和 AST SpaceMobile（纳斯达克股票代码：ASTS）刚刚向投资者提供了关于早期人工智能基础设施押注的两种截然不同的观点。

Oklo 公布了有史以来第一个季度收入 121 万美元。 AST SpaceMobile 印刷了 3152 万美元，但发射损失却高达 9 位数。 这两个故事都是关于构建人工智能时代所需的基础设施，但节奏却截然不同。

格罗夫斯面临严峻考验，BB7 重压天空

Oklo 的季度是由运营里程碑定义的，而不是损益表。 格罗夫斯反应堆在不到一年的时间里首次达到临界状态，此时散户投资者在 r/stocks、r/stockmarket 和 r/investing 上的看涨情绪得分达到 72。

收入超过 12 万美元的共识并不重要，更重要的是证明 Aurora 计划正在从纸质文件转向电力。 不过，每股收益低于预期 - 0.28 美元，而预期为 - 0.16 美元，这确实削弱了人们的热情。

AST SpaceMobile 的季度业绩看起来更为沉重。 收入下降了 8.36%，公认会计准则亏损为 -0.77 美元，而共识为 -0.29 美元，由于 BB7 发射事件导致的非自愿转换损失 1.259 亿美元，缺口达 168.01%。 然而网络仍在不断扩大。

首席执行官阿贝尔·阿维兰 (Abel Avellan) 告诉投资者，“我们的天基蜂窝宽带网络现已发展到 13 个在轨航天器，每一个都是近地轨道上最大的航天器”，蓝鸟 14、15 和 16 号已准备好发货。

地面原子与轨道天线

Oklo 出售电子产品。 其 Aurora 发电站设计从 50 MW 扩大到 75 MW，以吸引超大规模企业，其主要交易是与 Switch 签订 12 GW 的主电力协议。

首席执行官雅各布·德威特 (Jacob DeWitte) 明确地描述了这一时刻：“世界正在追赶我们一直以来所知道的事实：核电对于清洁、可靠和可扩展的能源未来至关重要。” 奥克洛建造、拥有和运营这些反应堆，这延长了兑现周期，但保持了长期经济效益。
